Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.

2. The present petition has been filed under Section 482 Cr.PC seeking quashing of Fir
No.0060/2019 under Sections 498A/406/34 Ipc registered at Ps Jagat Puri and all proceedings
emanating therefrom, on the ground that parties have entered into a settlement.

3.  The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that FIR was registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC but later on at the time of filing of the chargesheet Section 354 IPC was added.
4. Issue notice.
Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
She submits that since the present FIR is an outcome of a matrimonial dispute, the State has no objection, in case the FIR in question is quashed.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 21:18:16 5.

The petitioner no.1 (former husband), petitioner no.2 (father of petitioner no.1), petitioner no.3 (mother of petitioner no.1) and petitioner no.4 (sister of the petitioner no.2), as well as, the respondent no.2 (former wife) are present in the court and they have been identified by the Investigating Officer SI Rahul, PS Jagat Puri.

6. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 got married to each other on 06.12.2007 in accordance with Hindu rites and ceremonies at New Delhi out of the said Arun Sarna & Ors vs State G.N.C.T Of Delhi & Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16507405/
1 wedlock, two daughters, namely, Vaishnavi Sarna and Radhika Sarna were born on 27.12.2008 and 17.09.2014 respectively.

sentences.text: 7. On account of temperamental issues, certain disputes arose between the parties and they started living separately w.e.f. 09.12.2017 and since then the respondent no.2 has been residing with her parents.

8. Due to intervention of family members and well-wishers of both the parties, the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have settled their disputes amicably and accordingly, a settlement was arrived at between parties.

9. In terms of the settlement, it was agreed between the parties that they will get their marriage dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent by filing a joint petition under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
10. The parties further agreed that the petitioner shall pay a total amount of Rs.5,00,000/- in three instalments.

The first instalment of Rs.1,50,000/- was to be paid at the stage of first motion petition; the second instalment of Rs.1,50,000/- was to be paid at the stage of second motion petition, which have already been paid, the receipt of which respondent no.2 acknowledges.
11. The balance amount of Rs.2,00,000/- has been paid by the petitioner This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 21:18:16 no.1 to the respondent no.2 today in the Court vide demand draft no.266946 dated 02.05.2023 drawn on Punjab National Bank, Vaishali, Ghaziabad, UP.

12. The marriage between the parties has been dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent dated 20.02.2021.
13.

The parties have also agreed that the custody of the two daughters mentioned above shall remain with the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 shall not claim custody and/or visitation rights of the children.
14. The respondent no.2, who is present in Court states that she has no objection in case the FIR in question is quashed.

15. In view of the fact that the parties have amicably settled their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
16. There is also no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.
It would, therefore, be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings emanating there from.
